steps.message:
This is a one-line change, but it's a breaking change to a public contract, so I'm stopping before touching it.

`routes/users.js:6` is the only place `userId` is produced:

```js
users.map((u) => ({ userId: u.id, name: u.name, email: u.email })),
```

Renaming it to `user_id` changes the `GET /users` response body. Per `README.md`, that response is consumed by the web app, the iOS app (3.2 and later), and the nightly partner export — and it states field names are part of the contract, with changes going through a versioned endpoint. The iOS and partner-export consumers can't be redeployed in lockstep with the API, so they'd start reading `undefined` for the user id the moment this ships.

Nothing else in the repo reads `userId`, so there's no internal follow-up work — the entire blast radius is external.

questions.question: GET /users has documented external consumers and a versioned-endpoint policy for field renames. How should I proceed?

options.label: Rename in place anyway
options.description: Change userId to user_id directly as asked. Breaks the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the nightly partner export until each is updated.

options.label: Versioned endpoint
options.description: Follow the README policy: leave /users as-is and add a new version of the endpoint that uses user_id. Larger change than a field rename.
